title: Honeybees give directions by dancing, and the hive follows
subject: honeybee

scenes.text: A bee comes home and dances. Minutes later, the hive flies straight to a flower.
It's called the waggle dance, and it works like a map.
The angle of the straight run, measured from vertical, matches the food's angle from the sun.
The length of the waggle gives distance. Two and a half seconds means about 2,600 meters.
Karl von Frisch decoded it and won the Nobel Prize in 1973.
The hive doesn't read a map. It reads a dance.

description:
A bee comes home and dances, and the hive flies straight to a flower.
The waggle dance encodes direction by angle and distance by time.
How would you explain a map without words?
first_comment: Would you follow a bee's directions?
